commits.summary: Example 290: vulnerable-security is refuted in a probe at the frozen bound with a model of ArrayList the check asks for, and its job is queued (verification pending)
commits.body: 5.8.4 collects its matchers in ArrayLists on every path, and jvmcontract's own checker stopped at new ArrayList(int). The checker now has a model of java.util.ArrayList that it runs only for a check that asks for it (prove --model java.util.ArrayList; lib/models/java/util/lists/ArrayList.java, models::ON_REQUEST, ClassPath::runs_model): both constructors, size, isEmpty, get, add, addAll, both toArray and a fail-fast iterator; any other method is the JDK call it names. It is on request and not run for every check because new ArrayList(int) is the gap the contract library, the conformance corpus and the examples' recorded refusals are written about: without the option nothing changes. A result states the model where a path ran it; JBMC, --cache and a class with no model on request are refused. Arrays.copyOf of an array of references, which the model grows by, is modelled for every check, as it was for arrays of numbers.

commits.summary: Example 290: preservation is established in a probe at the frozen bound, the previous version's questions by name answered on its own class path; one job for all four tasks is queued (verification pending)
commits.body:
preservation (the release pair 5.8.4 to 5.8.5 through the adapter entry) needed four things of the verifier, each now there. (1) In a regression check made as a property of the pair of versions the previous version's classes are copies under the package before, and a question its code asks by a name it computes was answered from the program's class path, the new version's: Class.forName called by a copy now finds the copy of the class named and no class only the new version has, and a copy's getName() is the class's own name (lib/src/relocate.rs Previous, lib/src/bmc/runtime.rs). 5.8.4's initializer asks this way whether Spring MVC is present. (2) jvmcontract equivalence takes --observed-initializer and --model for such a check; an initializer is observed in each version that has the class, on that version's own class path, and the result says which. (3) new ConcurrentHashMap() and new ConcurrentHashMap(int) make an object with no content, a negative capacity refused: the caches an AntPathMatcher's constructor makes. (4) proofs/prove.py observes two more library initializers, UrlPathHelper's and AntPathMatcher's, met only where a release goes on to make MvcRequestMatchers.

Verified inline: tests/pairing.rs has two versions of a library that return the same number only if each one's lookup by name, class name and observed initializer are its own, both ways round (verified), with the refusals; claims.M#cached proves the map's constructors against their definition and claims.Samples runs it on a JVM; the unit tests (288), claims (15), pairing (4), values, conformance, loops, object_strings and value_parameters pass; test_costs lint agrees; validate_example.py 290 passes. At the frozen bound of 8, proofs/prove.py preservation was established in 2.1 s (573 paths), and a control with a wider region that must agree was refuted on select(servlets=[1], ...), run on a JVM, where the fix changes the selection by design. The other three tasks give their recorded verdicts with the final script (4, 659 and 708 paths). Jobs: 20261117-012215-example-290-the-four-proof-tasks-through (all four tasks at one commit) and 20261117-012216-the-proof-tier-after-example-290-s-secon. vulnerable-security's own job, 20261117-000856-example-290-vulnerable-security-through, passed in 3.4 s (collected in onkqouut); its record in target.json follows with the others'. commits.summary: The default run takes 4.6 minutes where it took 16: Rust's test binaries and the Python files run several at a time, and a passed run covers what it left unread
commits.body:
test_costs.py run: cargo only builds the Rust test binaries (--no-run), and they then run several at a time (--rust-jobs, by default half the CPUs, at most 4, and one per 1.5 GB of a job's memory limit), the longest first by what each took the last time (kept in the target directory). The Python test files run several at a time too (--python-jobs, 3 by default, 2 in a job); a file that fails has its second run alone after the others, so two files that disturbed each other show as flaky. The proof tier still runs one binary at a time, and --rust-jobs 1 --python-jobs 1 is the run as it was. Measured on this machine: the Rust binaries 707 s one after another in the first job, 403 s three at a time under a six-CPU limit beside another test job (peak 3.4 GB), 230 s four at a time; the whole default run 276 s, 49 of 49 passed, nothing flaky.

Three Rust test files prepare their fixtures together and not one after another, with the same assertions: observations.rs's Box Office examples test builds its ten patched examples four at a time (the binary went from 146 s to 71 s alone) and keeps the Gradle build between runs under a hash of its sources, tasks and JDK; application_core.rs and application_core_joint.rs compile their nineteen fixture builds four at a time.

default_tests.py: a run in the pipeline's fresh export records which files nothing opened and which folders nothing listed, from their access times (one packed line in its log; 'default_tests.py unread JOB' lists it), and a passed run then covers a later commit that only modifies those files or adds and removes files inside those folders. lib/ always counts as read, a rename is never covered, and a filesystem without access times records nothing. A probe of the Python half in an export left 546 entries unread, among them the example pages, CLAUDE.md and the runtime page. 'default_tests.py flaky' counts flaky tests over the collected runs. sync.py adopt-logs takes a log as a hard link where it can. Verified by the default run above, which includes the new tests of each piece (stand-in cargo and made-up runs); the inventory has the eight new Python rows, added by hand as the handoff note says.
